questions.question: Which rules demonstrably improved quality, cycle time, reliability, or commercial outcomes?
questions.answer: 5 incident(s) carry a real preventive control whose verification passed; those controls are the rules with evidence of effect.

questions.question: Which rules are redundant or unnecessarily expensive?
questions.answer: No doctrine-cost telemetry exists. Rework that is attributable to a specific rule is not recorded, so no rule can be called redundant from evidence.
questions.basis: cycle_metrics records rework, not rule-level cost

questions.question: Which rules repeatedly fail in practice?
questions.answer: 2 incident(s) had a check that existed and still missed the failure; those checks are the ones to strengthen, not the policies they enforce.

questions.question: Which failures indicate poor implementation rather than a defective rule?
questions.answer: 5 incident(s) explicitly kept their rule unchanged and fixed the implementation instead.

questions.question: Which new risks or business requirements require a change?
questions.answer: No topic has the required number of independent signals yet; this is not evidence that no risk exists.

questions.question: Which safeguards must remain regardless of frequency of use?
questions.answer: The four founder-protected gates remain: evolution execute, capital reallocation, business retirement, and first/elevated-risk publishing. Rare use is never a reason to remove a safeguard.
